points: Q3 2026 results will show whether the Q2 acceleration — 14% revenue growth and 12% gross bookings growth — carried through the summer travel season; a repeat supports the long case that demand is more than a one-quarter rebound.
The print will reveal if adjusted EBITDA margin expansion continued after Q2; margin holding or improving is key because consensus already prices 31.6% FY1 EPS growth on a 15.3x P/E and a 0.48x PEG.
B2B was reported as growing nearly three times faster than consumer in Q2; Q3 will show whether that corporate and travel-partner mix stayed strong, underpinning the 15.9% FY2 EPS growth estimate.
Full-year guidance was raised in Q2; the November report will test whether management lifts guidance again or at least reaffirms it, which matters for the 17-up/6-down analyst revision trend.
Peer prints from ABNB, MAR and TRIP in early November provide a read-through on travel demand, pricing and regional mix; strength there supports the long setup for EXPE.
EXPE trades at a discount to the tourism theme — 0.5x theme median P/E and 0.4x theme median PEG — so the print needs to confirm the FY1 EPS estimate of $20.87 is achievable to support re-rating.
The Q4 2026 and FY27 setup depends on Q3 gross bookings momentum and any commentary on 2027 travel demand; sustained bookings growth supports the FY2 EPS estimate of $24.19.
watch: Gross bookings growth stays at or above the Q2 12% y/y pace — supports the long.
Revenue growth holds near the Q2 14% y/y pace — supports the long.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expands y/y or at least holds — supports the long.
Full-year guidance is raised or reaffirmed after the Q2 increase — supports the long.
